context: Sho visits the countryside with his cousin. Meets Tatsuya again.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: しょう、ようこそ、田舎、また、来てくれて。
lines.en: Sho, welcome back to the countryside. I'm so glad you came again.
lines.style: Warm, unhurried greeting. Patient pause after the name. Genuine pleasure in the voice — not performative. Slight rasp from age and country air. Whole-hearted, the kind of welcome that makes a child feel truly seen.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: おじさん、お元気そうで。
lines.style: Small, careful voice. Polite formality mixed with real affection — he means it, not reciting. Soft eye contact in the tone. A six-year-old noticing something true about someone he trusts.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: 今日、野菜、たくさん、持って帰り。
lines.en: Today, take a lot of vegetables home with you.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact kindness. Not asking, just deciding — the generosity of someone who has. Slight emphasis on 「たくさん」like he's already thought about what would help. Quiet certainty throughout.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ありがとうございます。お母さん、喜ぶ。
lines.en: Thank you very much. Mother will be happy.
lines.style: Formal gratitude — he knows the grown-up words. But underneath: genuine relief and warmth. The small brightness of imagining his mother's pleasure. A child being trusted to carry something precious home.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: いつでも、田舎、来てな。家族、ずっと、繋がっていけたら、ええな。
lines.en: Anytime — come to the countryside whenever you can. I hope our family can stay connected like this, always.
lines.style: Slow, deliberate opening. Settling into something he's thought about before. Gentle and philosophical without preaching. The final phrase trails with care — not sentimental, but certain. A quiet extension of the heart.
